speaker: Unknown
en: Vercel gets a lot of support volume, as you'd expect, and 91% of it we resolve with an agent.
zh: Vercel 有很大的支持工单量,如你所料,其中 91% 我们用一个智能体来解决。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of outbound we do with an agent.
zh: 很多对外触达我们用智能体完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the inbound qualification is done with an agent.
zh: 所有入站资格筛选都用智能体完成。

zh: 所以剩下的人力支持团队现在真正做的是在产品里找出真实存在的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then working really closely with the engineering org, in some cases writing PR to go fix things versus turning through tickets.
zh: 然后与工程组织紧密合作,在某些情况下直接写 PR 去修问题,而不是在工单里打转。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a great data science agent that you can ask at anything you would have sent to RevOps.
zh: 我们有一个很棒的数据科学智能体,任何你本来会发给 RevOps 的问题都可以问它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even sales, we've raised quotas every six months.
zh: 连销售也是,我们每六个月上调一次配额。

speaker: Unknown
en: You join a company like Vercel because you believe you're going to be part of building something more generational.
zh: 你加入像 Vercel 这样的公司,是因为你相信自己会参与构建某种世代级别的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly a big reason that I'm there is I want to go write the go-to-market playbook for this era.
zh: 我在那里的一个重要原因当然是,我想为这个时代写下市场进入(playbook)打法手册。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome to Grit.
zh: 欢迎收听 Grit。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Juven, partner at Kleiner Perkins, a show where we go beyond the highlight reel and explore the personal and professional challenges of building history-making companies.
zh: 我是 Kleiner Perkins 合伙人 Juven,在这档节目里,我们超越高光集锦,深入探索打造历史级公司过程中的个人与职业挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today on Grit, I'm talking with Gene DeWitt Grocer, the COO of Vercel.
zh: 今天在 Grit 节目中,我和 Vercel 的 COO Gene DeWitt Grocer 对谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gene spent nearly a decade at Stripe, helping take it from $100 million in revenue to billions, before leaving to run go-to-market at a company a fraction its size.
zh: Gene 在 Stripe 工作了近十年,帮它从 1 亿美元营收做到数十亿美元,然后离开去了一家规模只有其零头的公司负责市场进入(go-to-market)。

speaker: Unknown
en: We get into why she walked away from one of the most valuable private companies in the world, what it's like to take a 10 person sales team down to one person and an AI agent, and the brutally honest feedback that reshaped how she leads.
zh: 我们聊到她为什么离开这家全球最有价值的私人公司之一、把 10 人销售团队缩减为一个人加一个 AI 智能体是什么体验,以及重塑她领导方式的那些残酷而坦诚的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Enjoy the episode.
zh: 享受这一集吧。

en: How big was Stripe when you joined it?
zh: 你加入 Stripe 的时候它有多大?

en: And when you left?

speaker: Unknown

en: Why do any of this?

zh: 我是说,为什么,就像在任何领域,像顶级运动员,像他们,为什么 LeBron 还想打篮球?

speaker: Unknown
en: He doesn't need the money.
zh: 他不缺钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I think it's because you have a passion for the thing that you've been getting out of bed for, for, you know, however long that you're not, you don't feel like you've left it all out on the field yet.
zh: 我想是因为你对你一直为之起床的那件事怀有热情,你知道,不管多久了,你还不觉得你已经把自己在场上毫无保留地拼完了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, there are things I still would like to do to sort of feel professionally self-actualized.
zh: 你知道,还有一些事情,我仍然想做,来达成某种职业上的自我实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I'd be bored if I weren't working.
zh: 我想如果我不工作,我会无聊的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly going through the moment we're in right now, you sort of have a sense that you'd be, you know, quickly irrelevant if you aren't in the thick of it.
zh: 当然,置身于我们当下所处的这个时刻,你会有一种感觉,如果你不在最核心的地方,你会很快就变得无关紧要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, but I think a lot of it is just actually legitimately enjoying problem-solving, intellectual stimulation, the people that I end up being around, things I think about as a result of doing my job.
zh: 所以,但我觉得很大程度上其实是因为真的享受解决问题、智识上的刺激、我最终身处其中的这些人、以及因为我做这份工作而思考的种种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you actually enjoy it or have you told yourself that over time you enjoy it?
zh: 你是真的享受它,还是你只是随着时间推移告诉自己你享受它?

speaker: Unknown

en: Yeah.

zh: 但是,平均来说,我醒来时想的是我今天想去解决的事情。

en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

zh: 事实上,我经常在凌晨 2 点醒来,想着我想去解决的事情。

en: Do you actually?
zh: 真的吗?

en: I did this morning.
zh: 今天早上就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Come on.
zh: 不会吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But do you think, can I, like, maybe let's play this forward.
zh: 但你想,我能,比如,让我们把这个往前推演一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, let's imagine you had no job.
zh: 比如,假设你没有工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think you would still be the type of person that wakes up in two and can't fall back asleep?
zh: 你觉得你还是会是那种凌晨 2 点醒来就再也睡不着的人吗?

en: Oh, no.
zh: 哦,不。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's definitely work-related.
zh: 那绝对和工作有关。

en: Meaning you wake up and then your brain just can't turn off.
zh: 也就是说你醒来之后,大脑就是停不下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: And do you find that you loop on the same thing?
zh: 那你发现你会在同一件事上循环吗?

zh: 或者说,比如,对我来说,我从一个循环开始,然后我几乎有种独特的能力,可以接着跳到一堆其他让我担心的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, like, they're not actually that worrisome.
zh: 而且顺便说一句,它们其实没那么让人担心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just like, I then project my worry of this one thing onto, like, basically my entire life.
zh: 我只是把对这一件事的担忧,投射到基本上我的整个人生上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: All in one long loop.
zh: 全部在一个长长的循环里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's not one loop on one specific thing.
zh: 但它不是针对某一件具体事情的单个循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that make sense?
zh: 这说得通吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, totally.
zh: 哦,完全说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, for me, it depends.
zh: 比如,对我来说,这要看情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, sometimes there's something hard that, like, I haven't, like, seen the matrix on yet.
zh: 比如,有时候有一件难事,我还没看清它的门道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, like, basically, it's one thing where I'm just trying to think through, like, chess.
zh: 所以,基本上,那就是一件事,我一直在试图想清楚,像下棋一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in a lot of cases, it's what you're describing where it's like a set of things you're going through that again, when you wake up in the morning, you're like, I'm not stressed about any of those things.
zh: 但在很多情况下,就是你描述的那种,就是一堆你在过的事情,而且当你早上醒来时,你会想,这些事我一件都不焦虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I find them all to be tractable, but at two o'clock in the morning, for whatever reason, they do not feel that way.
zh: 比如我觉得它们全都是可以解决的,但凌晨 2 点的时候,不知为什么,它们就不是那个感觉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then maybe on this idea of like being bored and relevance and like quickly atrophying everything.
zh: 然后也许关于这个想法,比如感到无聊、相关性、以及一切都很快萎缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: If you were to like kick back after Stripe.
zh: 如果你从 Stripe 退下来之后想歇一歇。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: You would scratch your itch on like talking to entrepreneurs and all those things.
zh: 你会满足你的瘾,比如和创业者聊天之类的所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you know, you could do something like that.
zh: 比如,你知道,你可以做那样的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could advise companies.
zh: 你可以给公司做顾问。

en: I think you were advising Vercel before you decided to actually jump in full time.
zh: 我记得在你决定真正全职加入之前,你在给 Vercel 做顾问。

zh: 你不用处理任何人的 HR 问题,对吧?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 比如,你知道,为什么不那样呢?

zh: 我觉得我一直是一个硬核的实干者。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like my sense of satisfaction is tied to did I tangibly, you know, move the chains today?
zh: 所以我的满足感是和「我今天是否切实地推进了进展」绑定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I just get a lot more, yeah, satisfaction out of like I can at the end of this week be like there's something I can point to that had not worked this week would not have occurred.
zh: 所以我只是能得到多得多的满足感,是的,比如在周末结束时我可以说,有一件我能指得出来的事情,如果这周我没做它就不会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just a different way to value what you do.
zh: 只是另一种衡量你所做之事价值的方式。

en: At Stripe, after Stripe, were you considering not doing anything?
zh: 在 Stripe,离开 Stripe 之后,你有没有考虑过什么都不做?

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely not.
zh: 当然没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 没有。

en: I took three days off in between Stripe and Vercel.
zh: 我在 Stripe 和 Vercel 之间休了三天假。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you started advising Vercel while you were at Stripe?
zh: 但你在 Stripe 期间就开始给 Vercel 做顾问了?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: Stripe was very generous along those lines.
zh: Stripe 在这方面非常慷慨。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stripe obviously cares deeply about the startup community.
zh: Stripe 显然非常关心创业社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of the ways I think it allowed people to give back was broad support for advisorship.
zh: 所以我认为,允许员工回馈的方式之一就是广泛支持担任顾问这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 嗯。

en: And what year was that?
zh: 那是哪一年?

speaker: Unknown
en: How long have you been at Vercel?
zh: 你在 Vercel 待了多久?

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been at Vercel almost a year and a half.
zh: 我在 Vercel 待了快一年半了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that had started a year and a half before I came.
zh: 而我觉得那件事在我来之前一年半就开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at least three years ago.
zh: 所以至少是三年前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You took three days off?
zh: 你只休了三天假?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, my last day of work was a Thursday and I started on a Monday.
zh: 是啊,我上班的最后一天是周四,然后周一就开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: People, I think, misunderstand the toll of hypergrowth.
zh: 我想人们误解了高速增长的代价。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's like the faster you grow, the more taxing it is, physically, mentally.
zh: 我觉得你增长得越快,消耗就越大,无论是身体上还是精神上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not growing is also its own version of taxing, but like you do that as Stripe and then you join Vercel and then you're like right back on the bullet train.
zh: 不增长也有它自己消耗人的一面,但你在 Stripe 经历了那种状态,然后加入 Vercel,然后你发现自己马上又回到了子弹头列车上。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's been, how long, eight years at Stripe?
zh: 那是多久,在 Stripe 八年?

speaker: Unknown
en: Over nine.
zh: 九年多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nine.
zh: 九年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're basically in a going on 10, 10 and a half plus year consecutive run.
zh: 所以你基本上马上要连续跑满 10 年、10 年半以上了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of basically an all out sprint.
zh: 基本上是一场全力以赴的冲刺。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you feel?
zh: 你感觉怎么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it depends on like the given moment.
zh: 我是说,这取决于具体的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I remember when I was at Stripe and new people would join Stripe who similarly, you know, took maybe a week or two off after long term, very successful runs.
zh: 我记得我在 Stripe 的时候,有一些新加入 Stripe 的人,他们同样地,你知道,在长期、非常成功的奔跑之后休了一两周的假。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I always thought that they were crazy.
zh: 我当时总觉得他们疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I did the exact same thing, you know, even
zh: 然后我自己做了完全一样的事,你知道,甚至

speaker: Unknown
en: When I started at Vercel, there was a lot I ended up needing to transform, and that was very hard to come in and be new, make some, like, very substantial changes that were not straightforward to pull off.
zh: 我刚加入 Vercel 时,有很多东西我最终需要去改造,而作为一个新人进来,做一些非常重大的、并不容易实现的改变,是非常艰难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there were definitely points through that window where I was like, man, I should have taken time off because, like, my battery did not get recharged and I'm now probably utilizing it more than I ever have in my career.
zh: 所以在那段时间里确实有一些时刻我会想,天哪,我真应该先休个假,因为我的电池根本没充上电,而我现在对它的消耗可能超过了我职业生涯中的任何时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you come out the other side of it, actually,
zh: 然后你会从另一头走出来,实际上,

speaker: Unknown
en: Remember, we announced a bunch of changes exactly this week, last year.
zh: 记得吗,恰恰是去年的这一周,我们宣布了一系列变革。

speaker: Unknown
en: The day I announced them, I had the best sleep I had had in a year because it was like, okay, finally, I have been able to figure out what I thought was wrong, how I wanted to change it, actually get a group of people to go make those changes, and at least this first step has landed.
zh: 我宣布的那天,我睡了一年来最好的一觉,因为感觉是,好了,终于,我已经想清楚我认为哪里出了问题、我想怎么改变它,真正让一群人去做出那些改变,而这第一步至少已经落地了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, and then you come out the other side and like, you know, I think things, you have peaks and valleys where like you've got weeks, I can't wait to jump out of bed.
zh: 你知道,然后你从另一头走出来,我觉得事情,你有高峰也有低谷,有些周,我迫不及待地想跳下床。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're launching something cool.
zh: 我们要发布一个很酷的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're getting something else out of the gates.
zh: 我们又要把另一个东西推出门了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then other ones where, you know, there's something else that's either zapping your energy or tough about this particular week, but tend to come out the other side and back up again.
zh: 然后也有一些周,你知道,有别的什么在消耗你的精力,或者这一周特别艰难,但通常最终会走出来,重新振作起来。

zh: 你现在在 Vercel 的职责范围是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's the entirety of go to market.
zh: 是整个 go to market。

speaker: Unknown
en: So marketing, sales, field engineering, which is all of your technical sales roles and support partnerships.
zh: 也就是市场营销、销售、现场工程师,即所有技术销售岗位,以及支持合作伙伴关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I sort of like to say if it touches a customer and makes a dollar, it's my job.
zh: 所以我有点喜欢这么说:凡是接触客户并赚到一美元的事,都是我的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you have really good product market fit and you have technical founders, there tends to be, it's not explicit, but it is implicit.
zh: 当你拥有非常好的产品市场契合度,并且创始人是技术出身时,往往会有一种,虽不明说但心照不宣的,

speaker: Unknown
en: That like the product should kind of sell itself.
zh: 观念,就是产品应该有点自己会卖自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is manifested in a bunch of ways.
zh: 这体现在很多方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of which is like when a, you know, let's just say the average CRO's tenure is less than two years.
zh: 其中之一就是,比如说,一般 CRO 的任期不到两年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was also super helpful, right?
zh: 这也超级有帮助，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because like if I wasn't showing the trajectory of the whole year, I could have had the first two quarters be good and everybody be like, oh, this is great.
zh: 因为比如如果我没有展示全年的轨迹，我可能前两个季度表现不错，所有人都说，哦，太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then just like falling off a cliff.
zh: 然后就像坠下悬崖一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: But actually you could already predict that in the business if you did math.
zh: 但实际上如果你做了数学，你在业务中已经可以预测到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, and then again, we could have a conversation.
zh: 所以，你知道，我们又一次可以进行对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like I prioritized, I needed to hire a number of leaders.
zh: 比如我做了优先级排序，我需要招聘若干领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one I hired was the CMO because it was immediately obvious our top issue is marketing, pipeline, top of funnel.
zh: 我招的第一个人是 CMO,因为显而易见我们的首要问题是市场营销、pipeline、漏斗顶端。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got him in within 90 days and by the time we got to Q4, we actually had done enough to change some levers and we got, we just barely beat actually.
zh: 我在 90 天内把他招了进来，到 Q4 时，我们实际上已经做了足够的事去扳动一些杠杆，我们差一点点其实还超额完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if I hadn't done that, I probably would have prioritized other roles as an example.
zh: 但如果我没做过那个，我可能就会优先考虑其他职位，举个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you come in, first few weeks, you have your board meeting.
zh: 所以你入职了，头几周，你有董事会会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're like examining the business.
zh: 你在审视这个业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: The model does not make sense to you.
zh: 这个模型对你来说讲不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you approach that with, gee, you're a CEO?
zh: 你怎么处理那个问题，哎呀，你可是 CEO?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that's not...
zh: 因为那不是……

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not an easy conversation.
zh: 那不是一场容易的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not just gonna go to the board and like be like, hey, by the way, like, you know, this guy gave me this number and I just disagree with it or whatever, right?
zh: 你不会直接去找董事会，然后说，嘿，顺便说一句，你知道的，这个人给了我这个数字，我就是不同意它之类的，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you have to like kind of delicately, cause you also don't wanna make the founder feel like, you know, you're not signing up for, you know, like you're not in it with them.
zh: 你得，有点微妙地，因为你也想让创始人不觉得，你知道的，你不是在为……你不是和他们一条心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's delicate, right?
zh: 这很微妙，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe not, maybe it's fine.
zh: 也许不是，也许没什么问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Part of the reason I came to Vercel was, like, Gia and I had gotten to know each other for a year and a half.
zh: 我来 Vercel 的部分原因是，我和 Gia 已经认识了一年半。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so one of the things I did that not enough people do is, like, I mean, we had had extensive conversations about the business, what he thought was working, what he didn't think was working.
zh: 所以我做的其中一件事情，是很多人没做到位的，我的意思是，我们有过大量关于这个业务的对话，他认为什么在起作用，他认为什么没在起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I interviewed with, like, 12-plus people.
zh: 你知道的，我面试了大概 12 个以上的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I had points of view coming in.
zh: 所以我进来时是带着自己的观点的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, they walked me through board decks.
zh: 比如，他们给我讲了董事会演示材料。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it was very exhaustive of, like, I was super clear.
zh: 这是非常详尽的，比如，我非常清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: I picked companies for a decade.
zh: 我挑选公司挑了十年。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, he was super clear.
zh: 你知道的，他也非常清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want a leader who we're not going to turn over, you know, in a year's time.
zh: 我想要一个我们不会在一年内就换掉的领导者，你知道的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a super open kimono on both sides.
zh: 所以双方都完全敞开了底牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: I came in with G being, me being super clear G and vice versa, like, hey, I'm hiring you because I want you to come in and effect change.
zh: 我进来时带着 G——我非常清楚 G,反之亦然，比如，嘿，我雇你是因为我想让你进来推动变革。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, like, I didn't pick a different number.
zh: 而且，我没有另挑一个数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: We kept the number, and we ultimately got there.
zh: 我们保留了那个数字，我们最终达到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You did.
zh: 你们做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good for you.
zh: 干得好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I just exposed the risk at the beginning of the year.
zh: 是的，我只是在年初就暴露了风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I made a huge number of changes.
zh: 然后我做了大量的变革。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things we actually locked arms on was, you know, one of the things that's hard about changing go-to-market is people have quotas.
zh: 我们其中一件真正紧密协作的事情是，你知道的，改变 go-to-market 的难点之一是，人们有销售指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your livelihood is based on your attainment of those.
zh: 而你的生计是基于你对这些指标的达成情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can't sort of, on a random Tuesday, decide you're going to go change everything.
zh: 所以你不能随便在某个周二决定要改变一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's easiest to change a sales team sort of at the haves at the beginning of the year, obviously, or in the middle.
zh: 所以最容易改变销售团队的时机显然是在年初，或者年中。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can close out a plan, basically, which is what we decided to do, which meant that I made a bunch of changes four and a half months in, which was a little faster than I probably naturally would have done it.
zh: 你基本上可以关掉一个计划，这正是我们决定做的，这意味着我在入职四个半月的时候做了一系列变革，这比我本来自然会做的要快一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, at six months, we would have been in the middle of Q3 and that wouldn't have been workable.
zh: 但是，你知道的，如果到六个月，我们就会处在 Q3 中间，那就没法操作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, like, we all sat down as an executive team and locked arms and said, hey, like, we think I've come up with the right plan.
zh: 所以，我们整个高管团队坐下来，紧密协作，说，嘿，我们认为我想出了正确的计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think we're going to do this a little faster than we all necessarily want to.
zh: 我们认为我们会比我们所有人都希望的稍微快一点做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: That might actually cause some near-run downside, but we all believe in the upside coming out of it.
zh: 这实际上可能造成一些短期内的下行，但我们所有人都相信随之而来的上行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're going to...
zh: 所以我们要……

speaker: Unknown
en: Take a bet and go, even if it means like near run trough so that we're positioned to come out the other side and accelerate, which is also super important because I can tell you six months after I made a lot of those changes, I definitely was not sleeping well again.
zh: 赌一把，干下去，即使这意味着短期的低谷，以便我们能在另一边走出来并加速，这也超级重要，因为我可以告诉你，在我做了大量这些变革之后的六个月里，我肯定又睡不好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why?
zh: 为什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you can't perfectly operationalize everything.
zh: 我是说，你不可能把每件事都完美地落地执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So at a certain point, you've done everything you can to try to make it as clean as possible.
zh: 所以在某个节点上，你已经做了你能做的一切，尽量让它干净利落。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there are a bunch of things I knew weren't done.
zh: 但有一堆事情我知道还没做完。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a number of things that, you know, you roll it out and you're like, didn't think of that one.
zh: 有很多事情，你知道的，你推上线之后会说，没想到那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was definitely a little rough.
zh: 所以那段时间肯定有点艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: But another six plus weeks after that, it looked like the right change.
zh: 但在那之后又过了六个多星期，它看起来就是正确的变革了。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you were evaluating Vercel, what were you looking for?
zh: 你在评估 Vercel 的时候，你在寻找什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, what were the things that you keyed in on aggressively?
zh: 比如，哪些是你着力重点关注的事情?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I started my career at Google where I stayed for a decade.
zh: 我的职业生涯始于 Google,在那里待了十年。

speaker: Unknown
en: I left for a Series B startup that it didn't end up being a perfect fit and then went to Stripe.
zh: 我离开去了一家 B 轮创业公司，结果发现并不是特别合适，然后就去了 Stripe。

speaker: Unknown
en: What got me to Stripe was I realized when I left that company that I knew exactly why I had left Google, but I had not taken the time to figure out, well, why did I stay there for 10 years?
zh: 我去 Stripe 的原因是，当我离开那家公司时我意识到，我非常清楚自己为什么离开 Google,但我却没有花时间想清楚，那我为什么在那里待了 10 年呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I was trying to figure out, like, hey, I want to go spend, you know, 10 years at the next company, like, let me go really try to understand why I stayed at Google for 10 years.
zh: 所以当我试图想明白，嘿，我想在下一家公司也待上 10 年的时候，让我真正去理解一下我为什么在 Google 待了 10 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I decided that it was three things.
zh: 然后我认定是三件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One was it had very well articulated values that it truly used as like decision-making criteria that were part of the vernacular and they were like naturally aligned to my own.
zh: 第一是它有非常清晰阐述的价值观，并且真正将其用作决策标准，这些价值观成了日常用语的一部分，而且和我自己的价值观天然契合。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two was played in a truly large market with natural adjacencies, so you could be there a decade and there was always going to be something new and interesting to work on.
zh: 第二是它身处一个真正巨大的市场，有天然的相邻领域，所以你在那里待十年，总会有新的、有趣的东西可以去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then three, and this was probably one that I'm not sure that many other go-to-market people would have said in 2015, was that it had like an engineer's engineer.
zh: 然后第三，这一点我怀疑 2015 年的时候没有多少做 Go-to-Market 的人会这么说，就是它有一群「工程师中的工程师」。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, like Google had PhDs who were inventing things like, you know, always wanted to run through walls.
zh: 你知道，Google 有一群博士在发明东西，你知道，总是想撞穿墙壁那种人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I felt that, you know, I'd gone from working on Gmail where like launches with a gig of storage and everyone's minds blown.
zh: 而我感受到这一点，你知道，我之前在做 Gmail,一次发布带着一个 G 的存储容量，所有人都惊呆了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It took Yahoo over a year to figure out how to replicate that to, you know, now you're in 2015 and like average software engineer wasn't exactly building that type of stuff anymore.
zh: Yahoo 花了一年多才搞明白怎么复制那个东西，而你知道，到了 2015 年，普通软件工程师已经不再构建那类东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I wanted the ones that were gonna go, you know, build hard things.
zh: 所以我想要那些会去，你知道，构建困难东西的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was what led me to Stripe.
zh: 这就是把我带到 Stripe 的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I stayed there for a decade.
zh: 我在那里待了十年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I was like, okay, I think I might've gotten my three criteria right.
zh: 所以我就想，好吧，我觉得我的三条标准可能找对了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, and what had happened when I'd gone to Stripe was when I started to evaluate companies, I was like, huh.
zh: 然后我去了 Stripe 之后发生的事情是，当我开始评估公司时，我就想，嗯。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there might be, like, five companies on the planet that, you know, I'm interested in working for right now.
zh: 我觉得这个星球上大概只有五家公司，你知道，是我现在有兴趣为之工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the time, it happened to be Stripe, GitHub, Slack.
zh: 当时恰好是 Stripe、GitHub、Slack。

speaker: Unknown
en: I forget who else that I, like, interviewed Sarah Staley with.
zh: 我忘了还有谁，我跟 Sarah Staley 面试过。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good list.
zh: 好名单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good list.
zh: 好名单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, sort of, same thing.
zh: 所以，差不多是同样的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you look at Vercel.
zh: 你看 Vercel。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also had, like, really well-articulated values.
zh: 它也有非常清晰阐述的价值观。

speaker: Unknown
en: They could really talk to me about how they used them in onboarding, all-hands, performance reviews, like, across the board.
zh: 他们真的能跟我讲他们如何在入职培训、全员大会、绩效评估中使用这些价值观，方方面面都是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Large horizontal market, you know, the thing I said to G when I started and he asked me one of the reasons why I joined was, you know, I felt like in the fullness of time, every pixel on the internet could theoretically be built on Vercel.
zh: 巨大的横向市场，你知道，我入职时对 G 说过，他问我加入的原因之一是什么，我说，我觉得假以时日，理论上互联网上的每一个像素都可以构建在 Vercel 之上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's, you know, an outcome you can chase for a decade.
zh: 所以这是一个，你知道，你可以追逐十年的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you could see it, you know, it was getting into CDN.
zh: 而且你能看到它，你知道，它进入了 CDN。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was getting into security.
zh: 它进入了安全领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, it's now in AI.
zh: 显然它现在在做 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think I'm going to have some challenging go to market stuff to do for a long time.
zh: 所以我觉得我在很长一段时间内都会有一些有挑战性的 Go-to-Market 工作要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then also, I mean, it's just that it's a company of like entrepreneurs and inventors, you know, everything they do in open source, like they're building the stuff that other engineers are going to go use.
zh: 然后还有，我是说，这就是一家由创业者和发明家组成的公司，你知道，他们在开源中所做的一切，他们构建的都是其他工程师会去使用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I feel like, you know, I'll hopefully continue to be on the right side of innovation.
zh: 所以我觉得，你知道，我希望自己能继续站在创新正确的一边。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is this your first time owning marketing?
zh: 这是你第一次负责市场营销吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I did at Dialpad when I was there, had also like soup to nuts go to market, not support at Dialpad, but I would say this is the first time I'm owning it at a legitimate scale.
zh: 不是，我在 Dialpad 的时候做过，当时也是从头到尾负责 Go-to-Market,在 Dialpad 不包括支持，但我会说这是我第一次在一个真正有规模的层面上负责它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you like it?
zh: 你喜欢吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I do.
zh: 喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I'm glad I have a CMO who like, you know, does the actual hardware.
zh: 我是说，我很庆幸我有一位 CMO,你知道，负责实际的硬件部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊，是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Keith is fabulous.
zh: 而且 Keith 非常棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've learned a ton from him.
zh: 我从他身上学到了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I've always sort of felt that one of the things companies don't nail is
zh: 但我一直有一种感觉，公司没有做好的事情之一是

speaker: Unknown
en: The human-based customer experience is a product just like the actual product.
zh: 基于人的客户体验和实际产品一样，也是一种产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you have different chunks of it, like it's super common for marketing and sales and support to roll up to three totally separate leaders.
zh: 而当它被拆成不同的块时，比如市场营销、销售和支持分别汇报给三个完全不同的领导者，这是非常常见的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that you don't create an integrated experience, you often have like Venn diagram of strategy.
zh: 这样你就无法创造一个整合的体验，往往会出现一种策略上的维恩图。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like multiple times in my career, there's been different segmentation for support and sales.
zh: 在我的职业生涯中，支持部门和销售部门使用不同的客户分层，这已经发生过好几次了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think that's workable.
zh: 我觉得那是行不通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's similarly on between marketing and sales, you know, often where people are putting dollars versus where sales is putting people aren't perfectly aligned.
zh: 你知道，同样在市场营销和销售之间，你知道，市场营销投钱的地方和销售投人的地方往往并不完全一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now it's my problem to make sure that's one unified thing.
zh: 所以现在让这成为统一的一件事，就是我的问题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The reason I ask is like, kind of like how...
zh: 我之所以这么问是因为，有点像……

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like every engineer in the Valley right now wants to be a founder.
zh: 现在硅谷似乎每个工程师都想当创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also seems like every exec wants to be a CEO.
zh: 似乎每个高管也想当 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just a natural progression in, I don't know, Silicon Valley life or whatever.
zh: 在，我不知道，硅谷生活或者什么的里面，这就是一种自然的进阶。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I talk to people like Chris Degnan and Chris is like a CRO's CRO.
zh: 然后我和像 Chris Degnan 这样的人聊，Chris 是 CRO 中的 CRO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like he is through and through
zh: 就是说他从头到尾都是

speaker: Unknown
en: A salesperson, salesperson.
zh: 一个销售，销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: He just loves that.
zh: 他就是热爱这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's like, look, I don't want Frank's job.
zh: 他说，你看，我不想要 Frank 的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to do that.
zh: 我不想干那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do not want to do that.
zh: 我真不想干那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious what your reflection is on that.
zh: 我很好奇你对此的反思是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think for me, I haven't really ever wanted to, like in coming to Vercel, I was very clear what I wanted to be was number two, like a very strong right hand to a technical founder.
zh: 对，对我来说，我从来就没真正想过，比如来 Vercel 的时候，我非常清楚我想要的是当二号人物，做技术创始人的一个非常强的左右手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I so far haven't totally wanted to be a CEO.
zh: 到目前为止我还没有完全想当一个 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like taking a
zh: 我喜欢把

en: technical vision and turning it into something people are buying.
zh: 一个技术愿景变成人们愿意买单的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I also wanted to own enough of it that it really, you know, sort of the revenue outcome truly rested with my ability to drive that.
zh: 但我也想拥有足够多的份额，让营收结果真正取决于我推动它的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really hard to own it all because you can't point a finger at anybody.
zh: 要拥有全部真的很难，因为你没法把责任推给任何人。

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we don't have enough pipeline, that's my fault.
zh: 如果我们的 pipeline 不够，那是我的错。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't be like, I'm the CRO and that's marketing's fault or vice versa.
zh: 我不能说，我是 CRO，这是市场的错，或者反过来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I will say that it's definitely another layer of accountability.
zh: 所以我要说，这绝对是又多了一层问责。

en: If someone in your position comes to you for advice, which I imagine happens all the time, of working with a founder, have you done things that you're like, this is good for us?
zh: 如果有处于你这种位置的人来找你要建议——我猜这经常发生——关于和创始人共事，你有没有做过一些你觉得「这对我们有益」的事情?

speaker: Unknown
en: The question behind the question is like most, when an executive comes to me asking about should I work at this company and I ask them like what your priorities are for like how you're going to evaluate the company, my general advice maybe is wrong, but my advice, my opinion is the relationship with the founder is maybe 10 times more important than every else, everything else on the list.
zh: 问题背后的问题是，大多数时候，当一个高管来问我该不该去这家公司工作，我问他们打算用什么标准来评估这家公司，我的一般建议也许是错的，但我的建议、我的观点是，和创始人的关系可能比清单上其他所有东西重要十倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I just feel so strongly that your ability to work effectively with the founder is like such a core ingredient.
zh: 就是我非常强烈地感觉到，你和创始人高效合作的能力是一个非常核心的要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe you disagree or agree with that, but I'm curious, like, have you figured things out that you think are unique?
zh: 所以你可能同意或不同意这一点，但我很好奇，你有没有琢磨出一些你觉得独特的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: I do agree with that.
zh: 我确实同意这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I mean, again, when G and I were getting to know each other, like I talked about it, I was like, you know, this to me is a professional marriage.
zh: 就是说，再说一次，当 G 和我还在互相了解的时候，就像我说过的，我说，对我来说这是一场职业婚姻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, we're going to spend a lot of time together, you know, and so we've got to be able to have productive conversations to feel like we can disagree.
zh: 我们会花很多时间在一起，所以我们得能进行有成效的对话，要觉得我们可以有分歧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would strongly agree with that.
zh: 所以我非常同意这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think there are some things I figured out, but I wouldn't say I've nailed this either.
zh: 我觉得我确实琢磨出了一些东西，但我也不能说我已经把这件事做到完美了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think getting time together is really important.
zh: 我觉得，争取共处的时间真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not all founders are big believers in scheduled meetings.
zh: 不是所有创始人都很相信安排好的会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I joined, you know, I did not have a scheduled one-on-one out of the gates.
zh: 我加入的时候，一开始并没有一个安排好的一对一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was like, we will have a scheduled one-on-one.
zh: 我就说，我们必须有一个安排好的一对一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I'm in a customer-facing role.
zh: 我是一个面向客户的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: I take meetings for nine-plus hours a day.
zh: 我每天要开九个多小时会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, like, I can't just find you serendipitously in the hallway.
zh: 所以，我没法在走廊里碰巧偶遇你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I need dedicated gene-gee time to discuss things.
zh: 我需要有专门的一对一时间来讨论事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started, I should have done this way sooner, but getting dinner.
zh: 我们开始——我应该更早这么做的——一起吃晚饭。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was, like, a big unlock, too.
zh: 那也算是一个很大的 unlock。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why?
zh: 为什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a longer time period.
zh: 时间更长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two hours, you're going to naturally talk about other stuff, so it makes it feel less transactional than, like, I got a 30-minute one-on-one, you know, let's work through some stuff.
zh: 两个小时，你自然会聊到别的事情，所以感觉不那么事务性，不像那种「我有一个 30 分钟的一对一，来，我们把一些事过一下」。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I thought that was, like, more personal, more, let us get into, like, other topics that, like, I think were interesting to both of us but would naturally get punted because they're sort of, like, important, not urgent.
zh: 所以我觉得那样更个人化，更能让我们聊到一些其他话题，我觉得那些话题我们俩都感兴趣，但通常会被搁置，因为它们属于重要但不紧急的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Um, I think, uh...
zh: 呃,我觉得,呃……

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, like, the way the broader executive team interacts, like, matters.
zh: 另外，整个高管团队互动的方式，也很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Vercel, like, core leadership team I think gets along better than pretty much any leadership team I've worked with, cross-functional one in my career.
zh: Vercel 的核心领导团队，我觉得是我职业生涯里合作过的跨职能领导团队中相处得最好的之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, super candid, non-political, just sort of, like, talks stuff out and really supports each other, which I think helps then, because you can also triangulate with, like,
zh: 就是超级坦诚、不搞政治，就是把事情聊透，而且真正互相支持，我觉得这也有帮助，因为你还能够通过他们来多方求证，比如，

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we seeing amongst ourselves any patterns in the types of feedback we're getting from founder, things that are top of mind, et cetera?
zh: 我们彼此之间,在从创始人那里得到的反馈类型上,有没有看到什么模式,比如他们最关心的事情等等?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's helped, particularly because also people have different relationships and different duration of relationships.
zh: 所以我觉得这有帮助,特别是因为每个人的关系不同,关系持续的时间也不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was the newest executive for a long time, trying to figure that out versus somebody who'd been there for three years.
zh: 有很长一段时间,我是最新来的高管,一直在试图搞明白这一点,而别人已经在那里待了三年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I don't know.
zh: 是的,我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I bet it's also very situational.
zh: 我敢说这也非常看具体情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: What works with one founder might not work with the next one.
zh: 对一个创始人在行的做法,对下一个可能就行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you do weekly one-on-ones?
zh: 你们做每周一对一吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Has anybody else been able to break in through his one-on-one calendar?
zh: 还有其他人能挤进他的一对一日历吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, I'll ask that tomorrow.
zh: 其实,我明天会问问这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a very sensitive subject for me right now because, like, I'm running a company and we're growing.
zh: 这对我来说现在是个非常敏感的话题,因为,呃,我在经营一家公司,我们在增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's just say, like, we're playing different growth games.
zh: 可以这么说,我们在玩不同的增长游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: But nonetheless, like, we're growing.
zh: 但尽管如此,我们还是在增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have, like, a leadership team and, you know, new managers.
zh: 而且我们有,呃,一个领导团队,还有,你知道,新经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would say I'm also the, like, anti one-on-one.
zh: 我得说,我自己也是,呃,反对一对一的那种人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mm-hmm.
zh: 嗯哼。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I hate it.
zh: 就是,我讨厌它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm like, just find me.
zh: 我就说,直接来找我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just find me.
zh: 直接来找我。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, like, just call me.
zh: 你知道,就是,直接打给我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I'm like, you know, what if we, what if you have something on a Monday, but our one-on-ones on a Wednesday afternoon?
zh: 我就说,你知道,如果你周一有个事,但我们的一对一在周三下午呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, are you going to wait for the one-on-one?
zh: 你会等一对一吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, like, but that's how we think.
zh: 你知道,但我们就是这么想的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: But then I'm like, okay, if you're not going to wait, then like, what are we talking about in the one-on-one?
zh: 但然后我又会想,好吧,如果你不打算等,那我们在一对一里谈什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Important strategic topics that need more time.
zh: 需要更多时间的重要战略话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, are we, you know, transacting on the thing right there?
zh: 还是说,我们,你知道,当场就把那件事处理掉?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, but, like, okay, what you probably do is, like, you just fire off a bunch of shit in Slack, and then I'm like, all right, well, that's not what I meant to talk about at 1159, and now I gotta figure out how to, like, take some complex thing that you've just, like, dumped in my lap and explain to you the context for, like, why what you think is rational is not, in fact, rational, which doesn't belong in Slack half the time.
zh: 是,不过,呃,好吧,你很可能做的就是,你往 Slack 里扔一堆破事,然后我就想,好吧,这不是我本来要在 11 点 59 分谈的东西,现在我还得琢磨怎么把你刚甩到我面前的一个复杂的东西,给你解释一下背景,为什么你觉得合理的东西其实并不合理,而这半数时候根本不属于 Slack。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Um, I, I think I would purport that you might be more effective if you picked what belongs in Slack in real time and, like, what might be, like, a more IRL substantive conversation.
zh: 呃,我,我想我可以提出,如果你能区分哪些适合在 Slack 里实时处理,哪些可能更适合,呃,线下的实质性对话,你可能会更有效率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's revisit the one-on-one thing.
zh: 我们回到一对一这个话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Uh, is the...
zh: 呃,是不是……

speaker: Unknown
en: I've gotten a sore spot.
zh: 我已经踩到痛处了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is the, um, is the, uh, yeah, I didn't like where that answer was going, so, uh, uh, is the, um...
zh: 是不是,呃,是不是,呃,是啊,我不太喜欢那个回答的走向,所以,呃,呃,是不是,呃……

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that founders tend to do is as executives and leaders come in, they have to like give up a part of the job.
zh: 创始人往往会做的事情是,当高管和领导者进来时,他们不得不放弃工作的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: But just like you, founders tend to be control frees.
zh: 但和你一样,创始人往往是控制狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as they give up responsibility, they start panicking because they're like, what is happening?
zh: 当他们放弃责任时,他们开始恐慌,因为他们会想,这是怎么回事?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they want to know what is happening.
zh: 他们想知道发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And no matter how good your communication cadence is or your systems of getting things, they still have this like weird thing where they want to like, okay, let's say they, like, yeah, like I don't need to project.
zh: 而且不管你的沟通节奏有多好,或者你获取信息的系统有多好,他们仍然有这种奇怪的东西,他们会想,好吧,比方说他们,呃,对,我不需要管项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to know, like, are you paying attention to like random details that I would pay attention to?
zh: 我想知道的是,你有没有注意到那些我会注意到的随机细节?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so like my version of the Slack dump is like, I'll just notice something.
zh: 所以就像我那个往 Slack 里倒东西的版本是,我会随便注意到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's just like one thing that like really bothers me
zh: 就是某一件事,某一真正让我烦心的事

speaker: Unknown
en: Bad grammar in an email.
zh: 邮件里的烂语法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bad grammar in an email, that could be one.
zh: 邮件里的烂语法,那可以算一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or, you know, hey, in the all-hands slide, I noticed that this person's title was software engineer, but it's an FDE, for example.
zh: 或者,你知道,嘿,在全员大会的幻灯片里,我注意到这个人的头衔写的是软件工程师,但其实是 FDE,比如。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like random things that actually don't matter in the business, like truth be told.
zh: 就是一些对业务其实无关紧要的乱七八糟的事,说实话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like, there's just this thing, it's like a tick.
zh: 但就是有这么个东西,像一种小毛病。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where I'm just like, I need to make it known that I'm paying attention to these things and care.
zh: 我就是会觉得,我需要让人知道我在关注这些事并且在意。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like, I'm not on the receiving end of those things.
zh: 但我并不是这些事的承受方。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have been.
zh: 我曾经是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I was on the receiving end of those things, I'm like, this is so annoying.
zh: 当我处于承受方的时候,我就觉得,这也太烦人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because usually the tone in which it is sent is not the tone in which it is received.
zh: 因为通常发出它时的语气和收到它时的语气不是一回事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Meaning when I receive it,
zh: 意思是当我收到它时,

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that I receive it is like drop everything and like he or she is pissed.
zh: 我接收到的方式就是:放下一切,他或她怒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, you know, all hell's breaking loose.
zh: 就好像,你知道,天要塌了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I send it, it's like, I'm just sending it.
zh: 而当我发出它的时候,就是,我只是随手发一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like one of a million things that I'm kind of sending.
zh: 这就是我发出的上百万件事中的一件。

speaker: Unknown
en: I expect a response, but I don't expect it to be received in the way that I am feeling when I send it.
zh: 我期待一个回复,但我不期待它被以一种和我发送时的感受一样的方式接收。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does the tee up make sense?
zh: 这个铺垫说得通吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am on the receiving end of feedback like you likely send.
zh: 我处在你会大概率发出那种反馈的承受端。

speaker: Unknown
en: And have you figured out a way to navigate that effectively without it ruining your life every time you get one of those messages?
zh: 那你有没有找到一种有效应对的方式,不会每次收到那种消息就觉得生活被毁掉?

speaker: Unknown
en: It has its moments.
zh: 它有时候还是会有的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so, I mean, maybe this is an example of things one can be good at in working as a founder.
zh: 好吧,我是说,也许这就是作为创始人工作中可以擅长的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are a set of things where you get good at being, like, herd chief.
zh: 我认为有一类事情,你会变得擅长当,怎么说,领头人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I'm on it.
zh: 比如,我在处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: Act.
zh: 行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, like, I'm not on that right now because I'm trying to do something that's going to go build a billion-dollar business and this misplaced semicolon I will deal with in the fullness of time.
zh: 但我现在不处理那个,因为我正在努力做一件能建成一家十亿美元生意的事,而这个放错位置的分号我会在时机成熟时处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you point out bad grammar in emails, you know, three times in two weeks, and I'm like, hmm, systemic problem.
zh: 但如果你在两周内三次指出邮件里的语法错误,我就会想,嗯,系统性问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we suck at grammar, right?
zh: 比如我们语法很烂,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So like what I'm trying to discern is like signal from noise.
zh: 所以我努力辨别的是信号和噪声。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, are there patterns to what you're saying that are actually indicative of a flaw in like my broader...
zh: 比如,你说的东西里有没有某种模式,实际上预示着我更广泛的……

speaker: Unknown
en: Function, set of functions, you know, or that like clearly indicates something you care about deeply that like may still be a P2 for me, but like at the end of the day, you are the founder.
zh: 职能、一系列职能上的缺陷,或者清楚地表明某件你非常在意的事——那对我来说可能仍然是 P2,但归根结底,你才是创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So either we're gonna have a direct conversation around why you think that's a P0 and I think it's a P2 and we can agree to disagree and go forth, you know, or sometimes you have to like...
zh: 所以要么我们直接谈一谈为什么你认为那是 P0 而我认为是 P2,我们可以各自保留意见然后继续前进,你知道的,或者有时候你必须……

speaker: Unknown
en: Check in on like, okay, is this really important?
zh: 去审视一下,好吧,这真的很重要吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not always easy to be on the receiving end of that.
zh: 处在那样的承受端并不总是容易的。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, in all fairness, this isn't just a founder thing.
zh: 顺便说一句,公平地讲,这不只是创始人才有的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I have a feeling that you also are on the giving end of this.
zh: 我感觉你也是发出这一端的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, I totally am.
zh: 哦,我完全是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that fair?
zh: 这样说公平吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not at the same order of magnitude, but yeah, I mean, there are a set of things that I'll get uppity about.
zh: 没到同一个数量级,但 yeah,我是说,有一些我会为之上头的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I try to have mine be at least like a little bit more thematic and know when to like let stuff go.
zh: 我尽量让我的那些事至少更有主题性一点,并且知道什么时候该放过一些事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you'd have to ask my team if they agree, but I think they largely would be like, there's a set of things that you can...
zh: 我是说,你得问我的团队他们是否同意,但我认为他们很大程度上会说,有一些事你可以……

speaker: Unknown
en: I try to have my behavior be predictable.
zh: 我尽量让我的行为可预测。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, like, in most cases, when I ping you on something, are you like, yeah, you know, that's one of the things she seems to care about?
zh: 所以,在大多数情况下,当我因为某事发消息给你时,你会不会想,yeah,你知道,那是她似乎在意的事情之一?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is it like, you know, constant deluge of whatever happens to be on my mind?
zh: 还是说,你知道,是源源不断倾泻我脑子里碰巧想到的任何东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, to be fair, the difference is that you get paid the big bucks to be able to basically deal with the deluge of unpredictable, unpredictable things.
zh: 不过,公平地说,区别在于你拿大钱就是为了能基本应付这些不可预测之事的倾泻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas your team should expect something a little bit differently from you.
zh: 而你的团队对你的期待应该有点不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think so.
zh: 我觉得是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right?
zh: 对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's that fair?
zh: 这样说公平吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think so, because my job is to be an operator.
zh: 我认为是,因为我的工作就是做一个运营者。

speaker: Unknown
en: An operator's job is to build systems that produce predictable output, basically.
zh: 运营者的工作基本上就是构建能产出可预测结果的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: For me, revenue.
zh: 对我来说,就是营收。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I need to make much more active trade-offs around this thing that bugs me.
zh: 所以我需要针对这个困扰我的东西做更主动的取舍。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it a P0 right now and moving us towards, like, whatever next evolution I'm trying to drive in, like, our system?
zh: 它现在是不是 P0,是不是在推动我们朝着我正试图驱动的、比如说我们系统的下一个演进方向前进?

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes, yeah, sometimes it is and sometimes it doesn't.
zh: 有时候,是的,有时候是,有时候不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes there are things that just bug you.
zh: 而且有时候就是有些东西会让你不爽。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I can't be sent a doc and not add commas where they belong.
zh: 比如,别人发给我一份文档,我没法不在该加逗号的地方加上逗号。
